facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he arrived at Kaluzhskaya Square to take part in the 'March of Millions' demonstration.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he walked with other participants from Kaluzhskaya Square to Bolotnaya Square.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered the meeting at Bolotnaya Square to finish early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
It took the police about two hours to clear Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
The applicant was arrested by the police on 6 May 2012 and taken to a police station before being released shortly after.
On 26 July 2012 the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having participated in acts of mass disorder on 6 May 2012.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected violence against the police under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 1 August 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence).

Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the organisation of mass disorder, accompanied by violence, riot, arson, destruction of property, the use of firearms, explosives and explosive devices, as well as armed resistance to a public official, shall be punishable by four to ten years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 3 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the instigation of the acts of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1, or the instigation of participation in such acts, or the instigation of violence against citizens, shall be punishable by a restriction of liberty for up to two years, or community service for up to two years, or deprivation of liberty for the same term.

Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the use of violence which does not endanger life or health, or the threat to use such violence against a public official or his relatives in connection with the performance of his or her duties, shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200,000 roubles or an equivalent of the convicted person's wages for 18 months, or community service for up to five years, or up to five years' deprivation of liberty.

A summary of the relevant domestic law provisions governing pre-trial detention and the practice of the domestic courts in such matters is set out in Zherebin v. Russia (no. 51445/09, §§ 16-25, 24 March 2016).
There were numerous clashes between the police and protestors at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered the meeting at Bolotnaya Square to finish early.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected violence against the police under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The Basmannyy District Court's detention order of 27 July 2012 referred to the gravity of the charges against the applicant.

The Basmannyy District Court's detention order of 27 July 2012 referred to information about the applicant's character, including a report by Moscow Police's chief of department at the Centre for Counter-Extremism.
According to the report by Moscow Police's chief of department at the Centre for Counter-Extremism, the applicant was an active member of organisations of a destructive character.

According to the report by Moscow Police's chief of department at the Centre for Counter-Extremism, if the applicant were to stay at liberty, he planned to threaten witnesses, abscond and obstruct the investigation.
The Basmannyy District Court concluded on 27 July 2012 that the circumstances gave sufficient grounds to believe that the applicant was likely to flee to avoid the investigation and trial.

The Basmannyy District Court concluded on 27 July 2012 that the circumstances gave sufficient grounds to believe that the applicant was likely to destroy evidence or otherwise obstruct the investigation of the criminal case, which was still at an initial stage.
The Basmannyy District Court's extension order of 24 September 2012 was based on the finding that the circumstances justifying the original detention order had not changed.
The Basmannyy District Court's extension order of 29 October 2012 noted that the circumstances justifying the detention order had not changed.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court's extension order of 6 June 2013 was based on the finding that 'no other measures of restraint would secure the aims and goals of the judicial proceedings'.

The applicant's request for an alternative preventive measure was dismissed by the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court on 6 June 2013 on the grounds that no other measure could secure the proper course of justice in the case.
